entries.n: Action Points, Magic Points, and Exhaustion Points
entries.lead:
[color=#8e171c]Action Points (AP)[/color]
Action Points are the central resource every creature uses to act. Swinging a sword, throwing an item, using a Weapon Action, Disengaging, and taking a Reaction all cost AP. Action points can be used to cast spells in the place of Magic Points (MP).

In combat, you gain AP at the start of each of your turns by rolling your Action Die. Class features such as Prowess can add to this. Any AP you haven’t spent by the start of your next turn is lost.

During Exploration, you instead have a steady 2 AP, which return after each action. 

[color=#8e171c]Magic Points (MP)[/color]
Magic Points are a fixed resource used only to cast spells. Each spell lists its cost in MP. MP can’t be spent on actions, and AP can’t be spent on spells during combat. Magic Points (MP) cannot be used to perform actions that cost Action Points (AP).

You gain MP through class features such as Channeling and Somatic Conversion, rather than from the Action Die itself. MP you gain stays in your Action Pool until you spend it or combat ends. MP isn’t generated during Exploration.

During Exploration, you do not generate Magic Points (MP).

[color=#8e171c]Exhaustion Points (EP)[/color]
Exhaustion Points represent strain on your body and mind. You gain them from effects, features such as Adrenaline or Sturdy, and spells whose cost includes the player gaining a number of EP, such as Cure Wounds and Rituals spells.

EP takes up space in your Action Pool like any other point, but it can’t be spent and is never lost to overflow. It stays in your pool when combat begins and ends and through unconsciousness. You remove EP by resting, at a rate of 1 EP for every 2 hours of rest, and some effects, such as Hearty food, can remove it too.

If your Action Pool is ever completely filled with Exhaustion Points, you die.

entries.lead:
[color=#8e171c]The Action Pool[/color]
Your Action Pool holds all of your Action Points (AP), Magic Points 
(MP) and Exhaustion Points. The combined total can never exceed 
your Max Pool.

[color=#8e171c]Overflow. [/color]If you would gain points that put you over your Max Pool, 
you choose which of the new points to keep and which are lost. For 
example, if you gain both AP and MP, you decide how many of each 
to keep.

[color=#8e171c]Exhaustion.[/color] Exhaustion Points take up space in your pool like any 
other point, but they can’t be spent or lost to overflow. If your pool is 
ever completely filled with Exhaustion Points, you die.

aka.ref: At the beginning of each Player(s), and Non-Player Character's (NPC) turn in combat, they roll an Action die, depending on the result of the die and the features that creature has, they generate that many Action Points (AP) for that turn.

entries.lead: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The numbers after it are the weapon's normal range and long range (for example, Ammunition 80/320). Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack. At the end of a battle, you can recover half the ammunition you used.

notes.t: Draft wording based on the SRD 5.1. Check it against Crawl's Action Pool rules.

entries.lead: Whenever the Camp Cook prepares a meal using a Cooking Pot or Pan, it becomes Blackened. A Blackened Pot can be scraped once to collect 1 Pinch of Soot, which cleans the pot.
Some attacks wound a creature deeply enough to make it bleed. While Bleeding:
fx: The creature takes 2 Bleeding damage at the start of each of its turns, and 2 Bleeding damage for every 5 feet it moves on its turn.
A creature that's Bleeding can spend 2 AP to hold its wound closed, taking no Bleeding damage from movement until the end of its turn.
Any healing from a spell ends the condition.
Creatures without blood, such as Constructs and Undead, are immune to this condition.
Creatures that regenerate each turn, such as Trolls, are immune to this condition.

entries.lead: Certain creatures and spells can impair a creature's sight, leaving it Blinded. While Blinded:
fx: The creature can't see, and it automatically fails any check that requires sight.
The creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls that require sight.
Attack rolls against the creature have Advantage.

entries.lead: A creature that fails to resist a magical enchantment can become Charmed. While Charmed:
fx: The creature can't attack the charmer or target it with harmful abilities or magical effects.
The charmer has Advantage on any check to interact socially with the creature.

entries.lead: When you craft this, record a message of up to 25 words in your own voice. Whenever the object is opened, it speaks the message aloud. You can choose for it to speak every time it’s opened, or only once before falling silent.
A creature that drinks this ends the Poisoned condition and has advantage on saving throws against poison for 1 hour.
A Bleeding creature that drinks this removes the Bleeding condition.
A creature hit hard enough, or caught in the right circumstances, can become Dazed. While Dazed:
fx: The creature has Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks.
The creature has Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
Whenever the creature fails a Dexterity saving throw, it falls Prone.

entries.lead: As part of a melee weapon attack with a [color=#8e171c]Blade[/color] weapon, you may expend 3AP to hurl a spare dagger or knife with a single precise deadly throw at a single target creature within 20ft of you. Target creature must roll a Dexterity saving throw with a DC equal to 8 + your Dexterity Modifier + Blades Rank. On a failed save, target creature takes 3d4 piercing damage and is inflicted with the Bleeding condition. On a successful save, it takes half damage.
entries.req: A [color=#8e171c]Blade[/color] weapon, as part of a melee weapon attack

entries.lead: Certain creatures and spells can impair a creature's hearing, leaving it Deafened. While Deafened:
fx: The creature can't hear, and it automatically fails any check that requires hearing.
Any spell that requires the target to hear a word, command or spoken phrase, such as the Command spell or any of the Power Word spells, has no effect on a Deafened creature.

entries.lead: A creature that has been submerged in water, or is soaked thoroughly with a liquid, becomes Drenched. While Drenched:
fx: The creature has Disadvantage on saving throws against spells that deal Lightning damage. If the spell uses an attack roll instead, the attacker has Advantage.
A creature soaked in water has Resistance to Fire damage. If it takes Fire damage from a spell that targets an area, it still resists that damage, but the water evaporates and the condition ends.
If the creature is soaked in a flammable liquid, such as oil or liquor, any Fire or Lightning damage it takes ignites it, ending this condition and making it Enflamed.
The condition ends after 1 minute.

entries.lead: This weapon can't be damaged by rust, acid, or sundering effects. This feature doesn't take up a modifier slot.

An item with the Enchanted property is a magical item. It counts as magical for the purposes of Detect Magic and similar spells and effects. The Enchanted property itself doesn’t make the item deal magical damage, though some of its enchantments might.

Enchanted is always listed last in an item’s properties, followed by a colon and the item’s enchantments. Example: Longsword (1d8 slashing, Versatile 1d10, Enchanted: Luminous, Searing 1)

Grants: Enchanted: Luminous, fills 1 open modifier slot
Grants: Enchanted: Searing 1, fills 1 open modifier slot

Simple Objects: Everyday objects that weren’t made from a recipe, such as boxes, lockets, cups, or tools bought at market, count as Basic items with 1 modifier slot.
A creature that is set on fire, engulfed in flame or set ablaze becomes Enflamed. While Enflamed:
fx: The creature takes 1d6 Fire damage at the start of each of its turns.
The creature can spend 2 AP on its turn to put out the flames, ending the condition.
Becoming Drenched in water ends the condition.
Creatures immune to Fire damage are immune to this condition.

entries.lead:
[color=#8e171c]Exploration[/color]
When you aren’t in combat, you’re in Exploration. During Exploration, time flows freely and players act whenever the moment calls for it. You don’t roll your Action Die during Exploration.

[color=#8e171c]Action Points (AP)[/color]. During Exploration, every creature has a steady 2 Action Points (AP). AP spent on an action returns once the action is finished. You can’t take an action during Exploration that costs more than 2 AP.

[color=#8e171c]Exhaustion Points (EP)[/color]. During Exploration, you gain Exhaustion Points (EP) only when an effect or a spell’s cost says so. EP stays in your Action Pool until it’s removed through rest, at a rate of 1 EP for every 2 hours of rest.

[color=#8e171c]Ritual Spells.[/color] Spells with the ritual tag can only be cast during Exploration. They take minutes or sometimes even hours rather than moments and casting them causes a spellcaster to gain Exhaustion Points (EP).

[color=#8e171c]Reactions.[/color] You can use a Reaction during Exploration if its cost is 2 AP or 2 MP or less.

[color=#8e171c]Lingering Effects.[/color] Spells and effects you start during Exploration continue into combat. If a spell requires concentration, you keep concentrating when combat begins. Outside of combat, one round lasts about 6 seconds, for any effect measured in rounds or turns.

Entering Combat. When combat begins, your steady AP and MP are lost and your Action Pool empties, except for EP.

notes.t: This is how AP, MP, and EP function outside of combat. This system is kept in place to keep specific edge cases from breaking certain functions.

entries.lead: A creature that eats this gains 1 extra slot in its Action Pool until its next rest or camp. This slot can only hold Action Points or Magic Points, never Exhaustion Points.
When you attack with a Finesse weapon, you choose whether to use your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

notes.t: Draft wording based on the SRD 5.1. Check it against Crawl's Action Pool rules.

entries.lead: This document appears genuine. A creature examining it must succeed on an Investigation check against DC X to notice it’s forged.
A creature that eats this has advantage on Constitution saving throws until its next rest or camp.
A creature whose safety is put at risk can become Frightened. While Frightened:
fx: The creature has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of its fear is within its line of sight.
The creature can't willingly move closer to the source of its fear.

entries.lead: A grapple is an attack that deals no damage but holds a target in place. While Grappled:
fx: The creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.

If a creature is Grappled by another creature, it can spend 1 AP on its turn to try to escape, making either a Strength (Athletics) check or a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check contested by the grappler's Strength (Athletics) check. On a success, the condition ends.
The condition ends if the grappler becomes Incapacitated.
The condition ends if an effect moves the Grappled creature out of the grappler's reach, such as being thrown or pushed away.

entries.lead: A creature that eats this during a rest or at camp removes 1 Exhaustion Point. If it has no Exhaustion Points, it instead regains hit points equal to the cook’s Cooking Rank.
A creature that is impaired and unable to use certain limbs or act clearly becomes Incapacitated. While Incapacitated:
fx: The creature can't spend AP or MP, and it can't take reactions.
At the start of its turn, the creature can't roll its Action Die.
The creature can't gain Action Points (AP) or Magic Points (MP).

entries.lead: An Invisible creature can't be seen by normal means, without the aid of magic or a special sense. Its location can still be detected by any noise it makes or tracks it leaves. While Invisible:
fx: Attack rolls against the creature have Disadvantage.
The creature's attack rolls have Advantage.
For the purpose of hiding, the creature is heavily obscured.

When a creature tries to locate a nearby Invisible creature, the Invisible creature makes a Dexterity (Stealth) check against the searcher's Passive Perception. On a failure, its location is revealed.

entries.lead: A Light weapon is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for fighting with a weapon in each hand.

notes.t: Draft wording based on the SRD 5.1. Check it against Crawl's Action Pool rules.

entries.lead: This weapon weighs half as much, never rots or warps, and mends itself of mundane damage over a long rest. This feature doesn’t take up a modifier slot.
As a free action, you can speak this weapon’s Command Word to make it shed bright light in a 20 ft. radius and dim light for an additional 20 ft., or speak it again to stop.

During a rest, while the party is at camp, the party designates one member to be the Camp Cook. The cook can prepare one meal, and the recipe determines how many servings it makes. The cook decides who receives each serving. Player Characters and Allies can only benefit from one meal per rest.

Every item has modifier slots based on the Tier badge of its recipe: Basic items have 1 slot, Advanced items have 2, and Mastery items have 3.

[color=#8e171c]At Creation[/color]: If your crafting roll meets the TC, you can add a modifier to an open slot. You can also choose to leave the slot open.

[color=#8e171c]Filling Slots Later[/color]: An open slot can be filled later with an Enchantment Modifier or a Craftable Modifier, such as Silvered Edge.

[color=#8e171c]Mundane by Default[/color]: Most modifiers are mundane bonuses or features. An item with modifiers isn’t magical unless a modifier specifically says it is.

[color=#8e171c]Innate Properties[/color]: Anything listed in a recipe’s Yield line when the item is created is an innate property, and doesn’t count toward its modifier slots.
Monster recipes are difficult to prepare. If your crafting roll fails the DC, the meal is ruined and the ingredients are lost.
A creature can be Muted by many things, from magical spells to having its tongue cut out. While Muted:
fx: The creature can't speak, and it can't communicate through spoken language.
The creature can't cast spells that require a Verbal Component.

notes.t: spell cards in the Spell Compendium now list Components, so Muted blocks any spell marked Verbal.

entries.lead: A creature that eats this during a rest or at camp regains hit points equal to the cook’s Cooking Rank.
Paralysis can be caused by many things, from a creature's toxic venom to a wizard's spell. While Paralyzed:
fx: The creature is Incapacitated (see the condition), and it can't move or speak.
The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
Attack rolls against the creature have Advantage.
Any attack that hits the creature is a critical hit if the attacker is within 5 feet of it.

notes.t: effects that cause Paralyzed define their own duration or a saving throw that repeats without an AP cost, since an Incapacitated creature can't spend AP.

entries.lead: A Petrified creature has been turned to stone or another solid material. While Petrified:
fx: The creature, along with any nonmagical object it's wearing or carrying, is transformed into a solid, inanimate substance (usually stone). Its weight increases tenfold.
The creature is Incapacitated (see the condition), can't gain Exhaustion Points (EP), can't move or speak, can't age, and is unaware of its surroundings.
Attack rolls against the creature have Advantage.
The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
The creature has Resistance to all damage.
The creature is immune to poison and disease, although any poison or disease already in its system is suspended, not cured.

entries.lead:
[color=#8e171c]Combat Phases[/color]

[color=#8e171c]Initializing Combat.[/color] Combat begins when either damage resolves, a hostile or combative action resolves, or whenever a spell effect from a hostile creature resolves on a creature.

[color=#8e171c]Combat Begins.[/color] At the start of Combat all creatures’ Action Pools empty, except for Exhaustion Points (EP). Everyone rolls initiative. Turn order is determined from highest to lowest.

[color=#8e171c]Ambush.[/color] If a group of creature or players get the upper hand on an unaware group, the first round of combat becomes a Surprise Round. During a Surprise Round the attacking group and/or party gets to act first and all surprised creature cannot act until the round has resolved.

[color=#8e171c]Combat Rounds.[/color] In initiative order, from highest to lowest, each creature starts its turn by rolling its Action Die and gaining points (Prowess, Channeling and Somatic Conversion apply). It then spends points and ends its turn.

[color=#8e171c]End of Combat.[/color] When no hostile creatures remain, or every side stops fighting, all Action Pools empty except for EP, and everyone returns to Exploration.

Each round starts with the player and/or creature that rolled the highest Initiative, and a round ends with the player and/or creature that rolled the lowest concludes their turn.
[color=#8e171c]End of Combat.[/color] When no hostile creatures remain, or every side stops fighting, all Action Pools empty except for EP, and everyone returns to Exploration.

entries.lead: You can use a lockpick to make a Thievery check to open a lock. If the check fails, the lockpick breaks and can’t be used again. Without a lockpick or a similar tool, you can’t attempt to pick a lock.
A creature that has been exposed to a toxin can become Poisoned. While Poisoned:
fx: The creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

notes.t: Poisoned covers toxins, venoms and poisons. Sickened covers disease and nausea.

entries.lead: This food doesn’t spoil for 2 weeks and can be eaten during a rest or at camp without a Cooking Fire.
A Prone creature has been knocked down and is lying on the ground. While Prone:
fx: The creature's only movement option is to crawl, unless it stands up, which ends the condition. Standing up costs half the creature's speed for that turn.
The creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls.
An attack roll against the creature has Advantage if the attacker is within 5 feet of it. Otherwise, the attack roll has Disadvantage.

entries.lead: You can eat this outside of a rest by spending 1 AP, regaining hit points equal to the cook’s Cooking Rank. A creature can only benefit from one Quick Bite between rests.

While you wear this Sheath with a sword sheathed in it, you gain X additional Action Points at the start of your first turn in a combat. These Action Points (AP) can only be spent on melee weapon attacks. You can only benefit from one item with the Quick Draw feature.

notes.t: Written for Quick Draw 1 on the Leather Sword Sheath: "you gain 1 additional Action Point". X replaces the 1 for other ranks.

entries.lead: When you take mundane damage, reduce that damage by X. You can only benefit from the Resist property on one piece of equipment at a time.
A creature that drinks this regains hit points. The amount depends on the item: 1d6 + 1 for a Minor Healing Draught, 2d4 + 2 for a Healing Potion, and 1d4 + 1 for a Bloodclutch Draught.
A creature can be Restrained by many things, from entangling spells to the webs of giant spiders. While Restrained:
fx: The creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.
Attack rolls against the creature have Advantage, and the creature's attack rolls have Disadvantage.
The creature has Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

notes.t: no default escape rule. Each effect that Restrains defines how it ends.

entries.lead: After you make a ranged attack with this weapon, it flies back to your hand at the end of your turn.
Holding this under the nose of a creature within 5 ft. ends the Dazed condition, or wakes it if it’s Unconscious but has at least 1 hit point.
A ruined monster meal can still be eaten, but any creature that eats it gains the Sickened condition until its next rest or camp.
This item counts as a holy symbol for any spell or feature that requires one.

You can spend 1 AP to scatter the caltrops across a 5 ft. square within 5 ft. of you. A creature that enters the area must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 piercing damage and end its movement. You can gather the caltrops back up outside of combat.

When you craft this, choose one spell you know, one language you know, and the scroll’s Rank (X). X can’t exceed your Scribing Tier’s maximum or your own Rank in that spell. If you meet the TC, X increases by 1. The spell is written into the scroll in that language. A spellcaster who knows the language can read the scroll to cast the spell, following the Spell Scroll rules. You must be capable of casting the spell in order to copy it to a scroll.
This weapon deals an additional X magical fire damage on a hit.
When you roll the highest number on this weapon's damage die, the target gains the Bleeding condition. This feature doesn't take up a modifier slot.
Each Cooking recipe lists how many people it feeds. If your crafting roll meets or exceeds the recipe’s TC, you make additional servings, as listed on the recipe.
A creature afflicted by a disease or overwhelming nausea becomes Sickened. While Sickened:
fx: The creature has Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws. Whenever a Sickened creature fails a Constitution saving throw, it loses 1 Action Point (AP) from its Action Pool while convulsing or vomiting.
The creature has Disadvantage on all skill checks.

entries.lead: This weapon counts as silver for overcoming resistances and vulnerabilities, such as those of lycanthropes, certain fiends, and aberrations.

A humanoid that drinks this must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or fall Unconscious for 1 hour. The creature wakes early if it takes damage or another creature uses an action to shake it awake. The brew is colorless and nearly tasteless when mixed into another drink.
Apply this to yourself or a creature within 5 ft. to end the Bleeding condition.
A creature can be Stunned by certain martial and magical abilities. While Stunned:
fx: The creature can't use Action Points (AP) or Magic Points (MP), can't move, and can speak only falteringly.
The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
Attack rolls against the creature have Advantage.

notes.t: unlike Incapacitated, a Stunned creature still rolls its Action Die and gains points. It just can't spend them until the stun ends (capped by Max Pool). A stun delays a turn rather than deleting it.

entries.lead:
[color=#8e171c]Targeting[/color]
Targeting describes who or what a spell, attack or effect is aimed at. It works the same way whether you’re the one casting or the one being cast at.

[color=#8e171c]Target. [/color]The effect is aimed directly at one specific creature or object. The caster chooses who.

[color=#8e171c]Target Area.[/color] Whenever a spell or effect covers an area, such as a cone, line, sphere or cube, and affects everyone inside it, you are considered targeted. Even though you aren’t the direct target of the attack or effect, being inside the selected area makes you a target of that attack, spell, or effect. If any part of the area overlaps a creature’s space, that creature is also considered a target.

[color=#8e171c]Whenever you target[/color]
When you cast a spell or use an ability, its card tells you whether you choose a Target or a Target Area.

[color=#8e171c]Target:[/color] you pick a creature or object you can see within range. Example: you cast Bane on the goblin chieftain.
Target Area: you pick where the effect goes, and every creature caught inside it is affected, friend or foe. Example: you cast Bramblesnatch in a 15-foot line from you. The two goblins in that line must make the save, and so must your ally if they’re standing there.

[color=#8e171c]When you are targeted[/color]
When an enemy’s spell, attack or effect is aimed at you, or you’re standing inside its area, you are targeted.

[color=#8e171c]Target:[/color] a goblin shaman casts Bane on you, or a bandit throws a dagger at you.
Target Area: a fire blast erupts nearby, and its edge reaches your square.

Any rule that says “when you are targeted” counts both cases. For example, Arcane Barrier can be cast whenever you’re targeted by a spell cast by a hostile creature, so it protects you whether a spell is aimed at you or you’re caught in its blast.

Each creature within 5ft of you must roll a dexterity saving throw with a DC equal to 8 + Your Strength or Dexterity Modifier + Swords Rank. On a failed save, creatures take 2d8 slashing damage and are inflicted with the Bleeding condition. On a successful save creatures take half damage.
This piece weighs nothing, makes no sound as you move, and can't be torn, stained, or soiled by mundane means. This feature doesn't take up a modifier slot.
